LESSON: SELF-EXPRESSION

Grade: PP1
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.2: Self-expression

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Self-expression. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their
2. Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: SELF-EXPRESSION
Subject: LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES · Grade: PP1
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Self-expression helps you succeed in LANGUAGE ACTIVITIES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: SELF-EXPRESSION
Study Self-expression like a learner textbook page: meaning → examples → practice → check.
Replace teacher words with your own words.
If a step is unclear, rewrite it shorter and try again.

PART 1: Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their

What this means
In this part you learn to Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Self-expression”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing

What this means
In this part you learn to Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Self-expression to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Self-expression is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Self-expression”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Self-expression to a partner. (skill: Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Self-expression to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their.
3. Practise this skill: Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Self-expression from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Self-expression: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a PP1 learner study Self-expression?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Self-expression means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: Use appropriate vocabulary to • Learners could be encouraged to express feelings and emotions in talk about how they feel and be school and at home. appreciated for expressing their.
5. Be able to: Use appropriate vocabulary to feelings and emotions express own needs in school and appropriately. at home. • Learners could be guided to sing.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.
